generations.memory_31: SMB signup flow simplification worked—we got +15% signups and +9% activation without hurting retention materially. The +4% qualified revenue lift is real but modest. Important: this didn't move the needle on other segments, so we're constraining rollout to SMB only.
generations.memory_44: Enterprise sales-assisted CTA is the right lever for the PLG-to-sales-motion bridge. We sacrificed some organic signups (-12%) but pulled in 24% more qualified leads and 18% revenue lift. This is enterprise-specific; don't try it elsewhere.
generations.memory_57: Referral incentives work well for mature accounts (6+ months in). +21% referral lift with +7% revenue and +2% retention bump. The mechanism here is probably stronger product-engagement and network effects among tenured customers. Worth scaling to this segment.
generations.memory_73: Deep discounting acquired a lot of SMBs fast (+31% signups, +18% revenue short-term), but the cohort fell apart at renewal (-12% retention hit). generations.memory_86: Streamlined onboarding shaves 2+ days off time-to-value and lifts completion by 13%. The +3% retention gain is small but in the right direction. This is a confirmed quick win; ready to ship more broadly.
generations.memory_91: In-product activation messaging is a consistent, modest lift across the board—+11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, +1% retention. Not flashy, but reliable and low-risk. Can scale.
